title: こきりこ節 (Kokiriko Bushi — The Kokiriko Song)
description: Said to be Japan's oldest folk song, originating in the remote Gokayama mountain villages of Toyama Prefecture. A 'kokiriko' is a pair of small bamboo clappers (seven sun five bu = about 23 cm) used as a percussion instrument. The song accompanies a slow, graceful dance with the distinctive 'ささら' (sasara — a bamboo split instrument) and features haunting nonsense syllables like 'デデレコデン' and 'ハッサノセーのセ' that date back to ancient agricultural harvest rituals.
license: Public Domain (Ancient traditional Japanese folk song from Gokayama, Toyama; pre-historical origins)
